text: Good tests avoid slow or unpredictable things like networks and databases — mocking fakes them.
A Mock is a stand-in object that pretends to be the real thing, but does exactly what you tell it.
Here we set the fake database's get_user to always return a fixed Alice record.
[chuckle] So calling it gives that data instantly, with no real database anywhere in sight.
[sniff] Mocks also record how they were used — whether they were called, and how many times.
That lets your test verify the code actually reached out to the dependency the right number of times.
[sigh] patch temporarily replaces a real function during a test, then restores it automatically after.
Here we freeze time itself, making time dot time return a fixed value so the test is repeatable.
[groan] Mocking isolates the code under test — you test your logic, not the flaky world around it.
